mechanism_narrative: Lower federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) compress discount rates and increase equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.0% (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 2.0% within a 3-month window, it signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.0% (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 240 and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1.5%, it indicates a high-inflation, low-rate environment that increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 240 and FEDFUNDS < 1.5 (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero returns).

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market expansion regime (HOUST > 1200 for 3 consecutive months), consumer confidence and economic growth are strong, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1200 for 3 consecutive months (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% for 2 months (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero returns).

mechanism_narrative: When the labor force (PAYEMS) exceeds 145,000 thousand persons and manufacturing output (INDPRO) exceeds 105, it indicates strong economic growth that may trigger a central bank response, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS > 145000 and INDPRO > 105 (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero returns).

mechanism_narrative: The level of residential sales (RSAFS) is positively correlated with S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, so higher RSAFS values lead to positive returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 400000 (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero returns).

mechanism_narrative: In a manufacturing expansion regime (INDPRO > 105 for 3 consecutive months), industrial output growth is strong, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 105 for 3 consecutive months (p-value > 0.05 from t-test against zero returns).
